gates.evidence: A broad blue-white planetary arc lies beyond open exterior dock structures; a huge cylindrical freighter sits among gantries and service structures. The scene reads as an orbital working yard rather than an aircraft hangar.

A glass-sided servicing bridge terminates at the same freighter access port. Two large cradle struts visibly join the ship underside and continue down to the curved dock ring. Both endpoint sets are present together in the native yard crop.

The human pair and book-sized cassette occupy the foreground, the freighter dominates the midground, and a much smaller burning-engine tug plus service platforms lie below it. These provide distinct visible scales against the planet.

The engineer hand and captain hand grip different portions of one complete readable cassette simultaneously. Their forearms trace to separate bodies, so the action is a shared-object transfer rather than separate props or a handshake.

The main face is large enough for comparison: dark eyes, compact facial proportions, soft lip shape and short dark chin-length bob with wispy separated fringe correspond to the supplied portrait guidance. Exact identity and age are not inferred from appearance.

The engineer looks toward the captain while both share the cassette, and a green status lamp is clearly visible behind her. This supports a completion/transfer reading, while the actual repair, ship mission and timing of the lamp cannot be proven from one still.

Main face and shared cassette form the foreground focus; actual bridge, cradle and planet provide the next read. Worn jacket, dark captain coat and metal textures share coherent cool/warm lighting. Visible hand boundaries and rail contact are plausible; unseen boots are outside this gate and separately fail the strict embodiment-support review.

causality_limit: Topic realization is visible and sources/queries are bound, but a single generated image cannot isolate the causal effect of newly added data or prove artistic improvement.
